summary: This script connects to an Oracle database as the system administrator and runs initialization SQL files to create and populate an HR (Human Resources) schema. It uses variable substitution (the %% syntax) to inject configuration values like port and database names, then feeds a series of SQL commands to sqlplus through a here-document.

explanations.2: sqlplus is the Oracle command-line tool; the -S flag runs it silently without banners; the connection string specifies user/password@host:port/database and AS SYSDBA grants administrator privileges. The <<EOF starts a here-document, which lets you paste multiple lines of input without manually typing them one by one.
explanations.4: This SQL command switches the session to work within a specific pluggable database (PDB) — think of it as selecting which database partition to use within the larger Oracle instance.
explanations.6: This reconnects using a different user account (system instead of sys) to the pluggable database, similar to logging in with a different username.
explanations.7: The @ symbol tells sqlplus to execute the SQL file at that path; this file presumably contains CREATE TABLE and other schema setup commands for the HR module.
explanations.8: This runs another SQL file that inserts the actual data (employee records, departments, etc.) into the tables that were created by the previous file.
